# Calisthenics Made Simple

No gym needed. No weights. Just your body.

This guide takes you from zero to pull-ups, one step at a time.

# The Grading System

Exercises are organized from easiest to hardest:

- Grade 4: Foundation
- Grade 3: Building strength
- Grade 2: Intermediate
- Grade 1: Advanced

# Grade 4: Start Here

**Straight Arm Plank**

Hold your body rigid with arms straight. Engage everything.

Goal: 60 seconds

# Pike Hold

Hips above hands, pushing up toward the floor.

Builds shoulder strength for future exercises.

Goal: 20-30 seconds

# Bodyweight Squat

Simple leg exercise. If it's too hard, sit on a chair at the bottom.

Goal: 20 reps

# Dead Hangs

Just hang from a bar and relax. Builds grip strength.

This is the foundation for all pulling exercises.

Goal: 30 seconds

# Active Hangs

Same as dead hang, but pull your shoulders down and back.

Now you're engaging your back muscles.

Goal: 30 seconds

# Scapular Shrugs

Do that shoulder movement for reps while hanging.

Slow and controlled. No rushing.

Goal: 8-10 reps

# Grade 3: Real Strength

**Incline Pushups**

Hands on a raised surface. Easier than floor pushups.

Goal: 12-15 reps

# Incline Pike Pushups

Same setup, but bent at the hips. Push overhead.

Targets shoulders.

Goal: 8-10 reps

# Inverted Rows

Lie under a bar. Pull yourself up.

1. Engage scapula
2. Pull elbows back
3. Lower slowly

Goal: 10-12 reps

# Jackknife Pull-ups

Feet supported, mimics pull-up motion.

A gentler way to build pulling strength.

Goal: 6-8 reps

# Lunges & Hollow Body

**Lunges:** One leg at a time. 10-12 reps per leg.

**Hollow Body Hold:** Back flat on floor, hold as long as you can.

# Grade 2: Getting Stronger

**Pushups**

The classic. Master these before moving on.

Goal: At least 20 reps

# Pike Pushups

No elevation. Just pike position and press overhead.

Go slow.

Goal: 8 reps

# Jump Squats

Add some power to your legs. Jump as high as you can.

Goal: 15 reps

# Pull-up Negatives

Jump to the top, then lower as slowly as possible.

This builds the exact muscles you need for pull-ups.

Goal: 8 reps

# Isolation Work

- Bodyweight bicep curls
- Sphinx pushups (triceps)
- Lateral raises

10-12 reps each

# Hanging L-Sit

Hang and raise straight legs to 90 degrees.

Great for core and hip flexors.

Hold as long as you can.

# Grade 1: Advanced

**Dips**

No foot support. Push your whole bodyweight.

Lean slightly forward for chest.

Goal: 8-10 reps

# Crow Pose

Balance on your hands with knees on elbows.

Introduces hand balancing.

Goal: 10 seconds (20 for advanced)

# Pistol Squats

Single-leg squat. Very challenging.

5 in a row is impressive.

Goal: 10 reps per leg

# Decline Variations

Elevate your feet for harder pushups and pike pushups.

More weight on upper body.

Goal: 8-10 reps

# Pull-ups

The goal of this whole journey.

Builds back, arms, forearms, and core.

Short-term: 5 reps
Ultimate: 10 reps

# Chin-ups

Palms facing you. Slightly easier because biceps help more.

Good stepping stone to pull-ups.

Train both for balance.

# Key Points

- Master foundations before advancing
- Hit rep targets before progressing
- Engage scapula on all pulling
- Slow and controlled beats fast
- Modify when needed

# Source

This guide is based on Kevin Zhang's video.

[Watch the original](https://youtube.com/watch?v=7RO-Fr6cXJs)

title: Complete Calisthenics Progression Guide
description: A structured bodyweight training system from absolute beginner to pull-ups, organized by difficulty grades with specific rep targets for progression.
---

## Overview

Building an impressive physique doesn't require a gym membership or expensive equipment. This comprehensive guide presents a structured calisthenics progression system that takes you from zero strength to performing pull-ups, using only your bodyweight.

The system uses a grading framework (Grade 4 to Grade 1) that organizes exercises from easiest to hardest. Each grade builds the foundation for the next, with specific rep or hold targets that signal when you're ready to progress. This methodical approach prevents the common mistake of jumping to advanced exercises before developing the prerequisite strength.

The key insight: mastering foundational movements like dead hangs and scapular shrugs is essential before attempting pull-ups. Most beginners fail at pull-ups not because they lack back strength, but because they haven't developed proper grip strength and scapular control.

## Grade 4: Foundational Exercises

These exercises build the base strength needed for everything else. Focus on mastering these before moving on.

### Straight Arm Plank
The simplest multi-muscle calisthenics exercise. Contract your arms fully, twist your elbows forward, and keep your entire body rigid. This develops pushing strength while also engaging core, quads, glutes, and shoulders.

**Target:** Hold for 60 seconds

### Pike Hold
Position yourself with your hips above your hands, actively pushing up toward the floor. This shifts more weight onto your shoulders, building the foundation for handstands.

**Target:** Hold for 20-30 seconds

![Straight Arm Plank](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/straight-arm-plank.jpg)

### Bodyweight Squat
Simple but effective for leg development. If you can't perform these due to knee issues or mobility limitations, use box squats instead—sit on a chair at the bottom to reduce range of motion.

**Target:** 20 reps

### Dead Hangs
The foundation of all pulling exercises. Find a bar, grip it firmly, and relax into the hang. Grip strength is the limiting factor for most beginners on pulling movements.

**Target:** Hold for 30 seconds

![Dead Hangs](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/dead-hangs.jpg)

### Active Hangs
Unlike dead hangs where you relax into your shoulders, active hangs require engaging your back by pulling your shoulder blades back and down (scapular depression). Imagine pulling your shoulders away from your ears.

**Target:** Hold for 30 seconds

### Scapular Shrugs
Perform the scapular depression movement for reps while hanging. Keep these slow and controlled—don't bob up and down. Quality over speed.

**Target:** 8-10 clean reps

![Scapular Shrugs](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/scapular-shrugs.jpg)

## Grade 3: Building Real Strength

This phase unlocks true bodyweight strength. You'll start developing a V-taper and building chest.

### Incline Pushups
Easier than regular pushups but still challenging. Focus on scapular movement: bring shoulder blades back at the start, keep them back through the movement, then protract (push forward) at the top.

As you get stronger, progressively lower your hand placement to increase difficulty. If you can't do 6 clean reps, start with wall pushups instead.

**Target:** 12-15 reps

![Incline Pushups](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/incline-pushups.jpg)

### Incline Pike Pushups
Same concept as incline pushups, but with your body bent at the hip so you're pushing overhead. This targets the shoulders specifically.

**Target:** 8-10 reps

### Inverted Rows
A pulling classic that works for beginners and advanced athletes alike. The technique sequence:
1. Engage your scapula first
2. Drive elbows back behind your body
3. Fully squeeze at the top
4. Lower slowly
5. Only then release your scapula

**Target:** 10-12 reps

![Inverted Rows](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/inverted-rows.jpg)

### Jackknife Pull-ups
Mimics the pull-up motion but with feet supported, making it significantly easier. Use the same form cues as rows: engage scapula first, drive elbows toward hips.

**Target:** 6-8 reps

### Lunges
Working one leg at a time increases the challenge compared to squats. Can be performed forward or backward.

**Target:** 10-12 reps per leg

### Hollow Body Hold
One of the best early core exercises. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor at all times—this ensures proper core engagement. Builds toward more advanced core work and helps develop the six-pack.

**Target:** Hold as long as possible with proper form

## Grade 2: Intermediate Development

At this level, you're building noticeable muscle and preparing for the hardest progressions.

### Pushups
The main chest builder. Mastery requires good technique and high volume. Getting really good at pushups unlocks many pushing variations.

**Target:** At least 20 reps

![Pushups](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/pushups.jpg)

### Pike Pushups
The non-elevated version of pike pushups. Same technique: get into pike position and press overhead. Go slow and controlled for maximum benefit.

**Target:** 8 reps

### Jump Squats
Add explosiveness to leg training. Focus on jumping as high as possible while maintaining consistent force across all reps.

**Target:** 15 reps

### Pull-up Negatives
The bridge between rows and full pull-ups. Jump to the top position, engage your scapula, then lower as slowly as possible while controlling the entire movement. This strengthens the exact muscles needed for pull-ups without requiring the ability to pull yourself up.

**Target:** 8 reps with good form

![Pull-up Negatives](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/pullup-negatives.jpg)

### Isolation Exercises
Single-muscle movements for targeted development:
- **Bodyweight Bicep Curls:** Use rings or a low bar
- **Sphinx Pushups:** Isolate the triceps
- **Bodyweight Lateral Raises:** Build shoulder width

**Target:** 10-12 reps each

### L-Sit (Hanging)
A fundamental core exercise. Keep legs straight, raise to 90 degrees, and feel your core and hip flexors activate. The hanging variation is easier and prepares you for floor L-sits.

**Target:** Hold as long as possible

![Hanging L-Sit](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/hanging-l-sit.jpg)

## Grade 1: Advanced Exercises

At this point, you're significantly stronger than when you started. These exercises produce dramatic results.

### Dips
The ultimate pushing exercise. With no foot support, you're pressing your entire bodyweight with chest and arms. Go as deep as your mobility allows with a slight forward lean to bias the chest.

**Target:** 8-10 reps

![Dips](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/dips.jpg)

### Crow Pose
Great for shoulders and introduces hand balancing, which opens the door to handstands and handstand pushups. Lean forward and put pressure on the base of your palm. The frog stand is an easier starting variation.

**Target:** 10 seconds (20 seconds for advanced)

![Crow Pose](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/crow-pose.jpg)

### Pistol Squats
The single-leg squat. Extremely challenging for balance and strength. Being able to do even 5 in a row is impressive.

**Target:** 10 reps per leg

### Decline Pushups & Elevated Pike Pushups
Elevating your feet makes both exercises harder by shifting more weight to your upper body. Decline pushups also emphasize upper chest. Expect fewer reps than the non-elevated versions.

**Target:** 8-10 reps

### Pull-ups
The culmination of all your pulling work. One of the best exercises for building back width, arm size, and overall upper body development. Also works forearms, core, and rear delts.

**Target:** Short-term goal of 5 reps, ultimate goal of 10 reps

### Chin-ups
Slightly easier than pull-ups because the biceps assist more. Learning chin-ups first can be a stepping stone to pull-ups. Train both for a well-rounded physique.

**Target:** Same as pull-ups

## Key Takeaways

- **Master foundations first:** Dead hangs and scapular control are prerequisites for pull-ups, not optional extras
- **Use rep targets as progression signals:** Don't move to harder exercises until you hit the targets for current ones
- **Scapular engagement is crucial:** For all pulling exercises, engage your scapula before initiating the pull
- **Slow and controlled wins:** Quality reps beat fast, sloppy ones—especially for exercises like scapular shrugs and pull-up negatives
- **Modify when needed:** Box squats, wall pushups, and jackknife pull-ups exist to help you build toward the full versions
- **Train legs:** Bodyweight squats, lunges, jump squats, and pistol squats ensure balanced development

---

title: Complete Calisthenics Progression Guide
description: A structured bodyweight training system from absolute beginner to pull-ups, organized by difficulty grades with specific rep targets for progression.
---

## Overview

Forget the gym. Forget the equipment. Your body is the only machine you need.

This guide lays out a complete calisthenics progression system that takes you from not being able to do a single pull-up to crushing sets of them. The best part? You can do every exercise at home with zero weights.

The system works on a grading framework—Grade 4 exercises are where you start, and Grade 1 is where the serious athletes play. Each level builds the foundation for the next, with specific rep targets that tell you exactly when you're ready to level up. No guessing, no plateaus, just consistent progress.

Here's what most people get wrong: they jump straight to pull-ups without building the prerequisites. Then they wonder why they can't do them. The truth? You need grip strength and scapular control before back strength even matters. This guide fixes that.

## Grade 4: Foundational Exercises

This is where champions are built. Don't skip this phase—master it.

### Straight Arm Plank
The entry point to calisthenics greatness. Contract your arms hard, twist those elbows forward, and lock your entire body rigid like a steel beam. You're not just working your arms here—you're hitting core, quads, glutes, and shoulders all at once.

**Target:** Lock it in for 60 seconds straight

### Pike Hold
Get your hips above your hands and push hard into the floor. This position dumps serious weight onto your shoulders, building the raw strength you'll need for handstands down the road.

**Target:** 20-30 seconds of solid tension

![Straight Arm Plank](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/straight-arm-plank.jpg)

### Bodyweight Squat
Leg day starts now. Simple movement, big results. Got knee issues or mobility problems? No excuses—use box squats and sit on a chair at the bottom until you build up.

**Target:** 20 clean reps

### Dead Hangs
This is the foundation of every pulling movement you'll ever do. Grab that bar, grip it like your life depends on it, and hang. Your grip strength is probably your weakest link right now—this fixes it.

**Target:** 30 seconds of pure hang time

![Dead Hangs](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/dead-hangs.jpg)

### Active Hangs
Now we're engaging. Same hang, but pull those shoulder blades back and down—that's scapular depression. Feel your back muscles fire up. This is where the V-taper begins.

**Target:** 30 seconds with full engagement

### Scapular Shrugs
Take that scapular depression and make it dynamic. Slow, controlled reps while hanging. Don't bob around like a fish out of water—own every inch of the movement.

**Target:** 8-10 crisp, controlled reps

![Scapular Shrugs](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/scapular-shrugs.jpg)

## Grade 3: Building Real Strength

Time to unlock actual bodyweight power. This is where your physique starts transforming.

### Incline Pushups
Hands elevated, body angled—easier than floor pushups but still challenging enough to build serious chest. The key is scapular control: retract at the bottom, protract hard at the top.

Getting stronger? Lower those hands progressively. Can't hit 6 reps? Start with wall pushups and work your way down.

**Target:** 12-15 powerful reps

![Incline Pushups](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/incline-pushups.jpg)

### Incline Pike Pushups
Same elevated setup, but now you're bent at the hips and pressing overhead. This hammers your shoulders with serious intensity.

**Target:** 8-10 solid reps

### Inverted Rows
The pulling exercise that works for beginners and elite athletes alike. Here's the sequence—burn this into your brain:
1. Engage scapula first
2. Drive elbows back hard
3. Squeeze at the top like you're trying to crack a walnut with your shoulder blades
4. Lower with control
5. Only then release the scapula

**Target:** 10-12 perfect reps

![Inverted Rows](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/inverted-rows.jpg)

### Jackknife Pull-ups
Feet supported, but the motion mimics a real pull-up. Use the same cues as rows—scapula first, elbows driving toward your hips.

**Target:** 6-8 quality reps

### Lunges
One leg at a time means double the challenge per leg. Forward or backward, your choice—just make sure you're hitting depth.

**Target:** 10-12 reps each leg

### Hollow Body Hold
One of the most underrated core exercises. Press that lower back into the floor and feel your abs light up. This builds the foundation for everything from L-sits to front levers.

**Target:** Hold until form breaks—then hold a bit longer

## Grade 2: Intermediate Development

You're building visible muscle now. Time to push into the harder progressions.

### Pushups
The king of pushing movements. This isn't about doing sloppy reps—it's about perfecting your technique and building serious volume. Master the pushup and you unlock an entire world of variations.

**Target:** At least 20 flawless reps

![Pushups](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/pushups.jpg)

### Pike Pushups
Feet on the ground, pike position, pressing overhead. Control is everything here—go slow and feel those shoulders working.

**Target:** 8 controlled reps

### Jump Squats
Add some explosiveness to your legs. Aim to get maximum height on every single rep while maintaining consistent power throughout the set.

**Target:** 15 explosive reps

### Pull-up Negatives
This is your bridge to the full pull-up. Jump to the top, lock in your scapula, then fight gravity all the way down as slowly as humanly possible. You're building the exact muscles you need without requiring the strength you don't have yet.

**Target:** 8 slow, controlled negatives

![Pull-up Negatives](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/pullup-negatives.jpg)

### Isolation Exercises
Time to target individual muscles for maximum development:
- **Bodyweight Bicep Curls:** Rings or low bar, pump up those arms
- **Sphinx Pushups:** Tricep isolation for arm size
- **Bodyweight Lateral Raises:** Build that shoulder width

**Target:** 10-12 reps per exercise

### L-Sit (Hanging)
Straight legs, 90-degree angle, core and hip flexors screaming. The hanging version is your entry point to the floor L-sit and beyond.

**Target:** Hold until you can't hold anymore

![Hanging L-Sit](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/hanging-l-sit.jpg)

## Grade 1: Advanced Exercises

Welcome to the big leagues. These exercises separate the serious from the casual.

### Dips
The ultimate upper body pusher. No feet, no assistance—just you pressing your entire bodyweight. Lean slightly forward to bias the chest, and go as deep as your shoulders allow.

**Target:** 8-10 deep reps

![Dips](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/dips.jpg)

### Crow Pose
Your introduction to hand balancing. Master this and you're on the path to handstands and handstand pushups. Lean forward aggressively and drive pressure through the base of your palms.

**Target:** 10 seconds (20 if you want to prove something)

![Crow Pose](/blog/calisthenics-anime-physique-guide/crow-pose.jpg)

### Pistol Squats
The single-leg squat. This demands strength, balance, and mobility all at once. Five in a row is legitimately impressive. Ten is elite.

**Target:** 10 reps per leg

### Decline Pushups & Elevated Pike Pushups
Elevate those feet and suddenly everything gets harder. More weight on the upper body, more emphasis on upper chest (for declines), more shoulder demand (for pikes).

**Target:** 8-10 reps

### Pull-ups
This is it. The exercise everything has been building toward. One of the single best movements for back width, arm development, and overall upper body power. Works your forearms, core, rear delts—everything.

**Target:** 5 reps short-term, 10 reps as the ultimate goal

### Chin-ups
Palms facing you brings the biceps into play, making these slightly more accessible than pull-ups. Learn both for complete development.

**Target:** Match your pull-up numbers

## Key Takeaways

- **Foundation first, always:** Dead hangs and scapular control aren't optional—they're prerequisites
- **Rep targets are your progression signals:** Hit them before you level up
- **Scapula engagement is non-negotiable:** Every pulling movement starts with scapular activation
- **Control beats speed:** Slow, quality reps build more strength than fast, sloppy ones
- **Modify strategically:** Box squats, wall pushups, and jackknife pull-ups exist to help you progress
- **Never skip legs:** Squats, lunges, jump squats, and pistol squats keep you balanced
